description: The CV adaptation / create-from-job modal reads correctly in every locale, meets contrast requirements, and behaves as an accessible dialog: focus moves in on open, Tab stays inside, Escape closes, and focus returns to the opener.

userStories.title: The modal's wording is correct in every locale
userStories.description: As a fr/de/it user, I want the modal's labels and help text to be typographically correct and to name the real button, so that the modal reads naturally and doesn't send me looking for a button that isn't there.
acceptanceCriteria: fr colons. Every label followed by ":" (match score, key gaps, strengths, reasoning, add skills, enhance) has a non-breaking space before the colon. de, it and en have none.
en unchanged. en renders exactly the same text as before, including "Add Skills: …" and "Match Score:".

de and it wording. de `enhanceSkills` reads "Erweitern", and the de character counter reads naturally (for example "(mind. 100 Zeichen: {count}/100)"). it confidence badges use "affidabilità", and `optional` is "(facoltativo)".
Help text. `createCV.helpText` quotes the real submit-button label in fr, en, de and it.
One source. All strings still come from `jobs.json` through `cv-adaptation-strings.ts`, and the locale-parity unit test covers every new key.
FR-1: No new dependency. Reuse a native `<dialog>` (like `mobile-sidebar.tsx`) or the existing focus-trap pattern (like `quick-add-modal.tsx`).
FR-2: en text unchanged. New strings in all four locales.
FR-3: Existing Tailwind tokens only.
Regression constraint: Every modal flow e2e still passes; only text expectations for W1–W3 and D1 and dialog locators change.
Regression constraint: The fixed-position modal still renders correctly on the phone detail (`job-search-mobile.spec.ts`).
Verification: The `CLAUDE.md` §14 baseline.

Verification: e2e: fr/de/it/en text checks for W1–W3 and D1 (fr colon preceded by U+00A0), plus a keyboard test (open, focus inside, Tab cycle, Escape, focus returns) from the editor and from Job Search at desktop and 375 px.
Verification: Measured contrast values recorded.
Verification: `ui-expert` (fr, de, it captures, focus ring) and `code-reviewer`.
FAIL condition: Any en text changes.
FAIL condition: Focus escapes the modal, Escape does not close it, or focus is not returned.
FAIL condition: Contrast below the thresholds.
FAIL condition: A dependency is added.
BLOCKER condition: A native `<dialog>` breaks the fixed-modal behaviour on the phone detail, and the focus-trap pattern also conflicts. Report it with evidence.
Out of scope: `ResumeSelectorModal`, which has the same issues. That is a separate item.
Out of scope: API error messages, the modal's flow, validation, requests and layout.
Out of scope: Other locales' wording beyond W2 and W3.

userStories.title: The modal is readable and keyboard-accessible
userStories.description: As a keyboard or screen-reader user, I want the modal to behave as a dialog, so that I can work in it and leave it without losing my place.
acceptanceCriteria: Dialog semantics. The modal root exposes `role="dialog"` and `aria-modal="true"`, and `aria-labelledby` points to its title.
Focus on open. When it opens, focus is inside it, on its first field or on the close button.
Tab stays inside. Tab and Shift+Tab cycle within the modal and never reach the page behind.

Escape. Escape closes the modal, from the input and from the preview stage, and focus returns to the button that opened it. This holds for the editor's "Adapt to Job" button, Job Search's "Adapter mon CV" and "Créer un CV", and on phones (the mobile job detail).
Contrast. "No content" has a contrast of at least 4.5:1 and the close icon at least 3:1. The close button shows a visible focus ring.
Unchanged behaviour. The modal's flows (create, adapt, preview, apply) behave as before.
FR-1: No new dependency. Reuse a native `<dialog>` (like `mobile-sidebar.tsx`) or the existing focus-trap pattern (like `quick-add-modal.tsx`).
FR-2: en text unchanged. New strings in all four locales.
FR-3: Existing Tailwind tokens only.
Regression constraint: Every modal flow e2e still passes; only text expectations for W1–W3 and D1 and dialog locators change.
Regression constraint: The fixed-position modal still renders correctly on the phone detail (`job-search-mobile.spec.ts`).
Verification: The `CLAUDE.md` §14 baseline.
